title: The Death of the Department Store
kicker: A data story · US retail sales · 1992 → 2026
subtitle: How one in ten retail dollars became one in fifty — and where the money went instead.
sourceNote: Source: US Census Bureau Monthly Retail Trade Survey via FRED. Seasonally adjusted, nominal dollars. Every number on this page is computed from that data.

defaults.title: Monthly sales, US department stores vs. online & other nonstore retailers
defaults.subtitle: Billions of dollars per month, seasonally adjusted, Jan 1992 – Jul 2026

steps.heading: $137 billion a month.
steps.text: That is what Americans now spend each month with online and other nonstore retailers — Amazon, mail order, direct selling.

state.label: online & other nonstore retail sales, July 2026

steps.heading: In January 1992 it was $5.4 billion.
steps.text: Twenty-five times less. Meanwhile, department stores did $14.1 billion that month — the anchors of every mall in America.

state.label: online & other nonstore retail sales, January 1992

steps.heading: Department stores peaked in January 2001.
steps.text: $19.9 billion in a single month. It has been downhill ever since — before Amazon was profitable, before the iPhone.

steps.heading: October 2004: the lines cross.
steps.text: Online and other nonstore sales passed department stores that month — $18.1B to $18.0B — and never looked back.

steps.heading: Then 2020.
steps.text: In April 2020 department-store sales fell to $6.2 billion — a level last seen in the 1980s — while online jumped 19% in two months and kept most of it.

defaults.title: US retail sales by kind of business
defaults.subtitle: Billions of dollars per year, 1992–2024

steps.heading: The whole cart.
steps.text: All US retail sales (excluding restaurants), stacked by kind of store. Cars, groceries and gas are the big grey slabs. Watch the orange and green layers on top.

steps.heading: As a share of every dollar.
steps.text: Re-scaled to 100%: department stores shrink from 10.1% of retail in 1992 to 1.8% in 2024. Online grows from 3.8% to 19.5%.

state.subtitle: Share of US retail sales by kind of business, 1992–2024

steps.heading: The rest barely moved.
steps.text: Cars, groceries, gas, building materials: their slices wobble but hold. This is not the whole of retail changing — it is one kind of store swallowing another.

state.subtitle: Share of US retail sales by kind of business, 1992–2024

defaults.title: Two months that changed shopping
defaults.subtitle: Change in monthly sales, February → April 2020, by kind of store

defaults.title: Four kinds of store, 1992–2026
defaults.subtitle: Billions of dollars per month, seasonally adjusted · each panel has its own scale

steps.heading: The accelerant.
steps.text: Between February and April 2020 clothing stores lost 88% of their sales, furniture 61%, department stores 43%. Online gained 19%. Groceries gained too.

steps.heading: It wasn't only department stores.
steps.text: Electronics and appliance stores peaked in May 2008 and are still below that peak in nominal dollars. Some kinds of shop simply moved online.

steps.heading: …while pharmacies and online kept climbing.
steps.text: Health & personal care stores are 5.5× their 1992 sales; online & nonstore 25×. Department stores are the only one of the four that ends below where it peaked twenty-five years ago.

defaults.title: E-commerce as a share of all US retail sales
defaults.subtitle: Quarterly, seasonally adjusted, Q4 1999 – Q1 2026

steps.heading: From 0.6% to 16.9%.
steps.text: The Census Bureau's own e-commerce measure: 0.6% of retail sales in late 1999, 16.9% in early 2026.

steps.heading: The pandemic pulled the future forward.
steps.text: The share jumped in 2020 and never gave it back. Every point of that line is a dollar that once passed through a store.

steps.heading: One in fifty.
steps.text: Department stores took one retail dollar in ten in 1992. By 2024 it was one in fifty-five — and in 2025 the Census Bureau stopped publishing the series at all.

state.label: department stores' share of US retail sales, 2024

footerHtml: Data: US Census Bureau, Monthly Retail Trade Survey, seasonally adjusted, via FRED (series RSDSELD department stores, RSNSR nonstore retailers, RSXFS retail excluding food services, and kind-of-business series RSCCAS, RSGCS, RSEAS, RSSGHBMS, RSFHFS, RSBMGESD, RSHPCS, RSMVPD, RSGASS; e-commerce share ECOMPCTSA), downloaded August 2026. All values are nominal dollars — growth multiples include inflation; shares and crossovers do not. "Online & other nonstore" is NAICS 454 (electronic shopping and mail-order, vending, direct selling). Kind-of-business series do not sum to the total; the remainder is shown as "All other stores". The department-store series was discontinued after March 2025, so annual charts end in 2024.
